source-integrity.sourceIndependence: primary SEC/issuer plus existing independent expectations context

company-underwriting.operatingTrajectory: Q2 FY2027 revenue $771.8M +30% YoY; Atlas +29%; GAAP operating income turned positive; RPO +91%; FY guidance raised.
company-underwriting.balanceSheet: $2.4B cash/investments/restricted cash; Q2 operating cash flow $141.9M and FCF $137.6M.
company-underwriting.capitalAllocation: Six-month SBC $286.8M and $200.3M share repurchases create a material per-share conversion consideration.
company-underwriting.catalysts: Investor Day Sep 29 2026; raised FY2027 guidance; AI workload adoption optionality.
company-underwriting.risks: Hyperscaler/native database substitution, consumption variability, high SBC and expectation sensitivity.

thesisQuality.basis: 30% revenue growth, 91% RPO growth and broad Atlas/EA adoption support durable developer data-platform demand, tempered by strong substitutes.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Revenue +30%, GAAP operating income positive, Q2 FCF $137.6M, $2.4B liquidity and raised guidance indicate strong operating momentum.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Strong growth is established but current source set does not prove favorable valuation headroom; SBC and expectation sensitivity warrant a weak-to-mixed conservative value.

catalystScore.basis: Raised FY2027 guidance and Sep. 29 Investor Day provide identifiable near-term checkpoints, while AI monetization remains partly unproven.

governancePower.basis: Improved profitability and repurchases show execution/capital return, but very high SBC remains a material alignment and per-share conversion concern.

alignment2036.basis: Operational databases are foundational to conventional and AI applications across industries, giving durable infrastructure relevance.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Atlas and Enterprise Advanced both grew strongly and serve geographically diverse application workloads using the same core data platform.

bottleneckControl.basis: Developer adoption and managed data services create switching friction, but hyperscalers and alternative databases limit control of the underlying infrastructure bottleneck.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Demand spans conventional and AI workloads and multiple geographies, though usage-based Atlas consumption is exposed to customer workload cycles.

substitutionResilience.basis: Document-model fit and developer ecosystem support persistence, but hyperscaler-native, relational and open-source alternatives remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Software delivery avoids physical supply-chain concentration and run-anywhere positioning spans cloud/on-premise environments, though cloud infrastructure dependencies remain.

pricingPower.basis: 74% GAAP gross margin and strong subscription/RPO growth indicate meaningful value capture, but consumption sensitivity and competition limit a stronger conclusion.

riskEvidence.basis: Material risks include cloud consumption variability, hyperscaler/native database competition, high SBC dilution and AI/valuation expectation sensitivity.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Fresh issuer and SEC results directly establish growth, cash flow, RPO and SBC; independent context exists, while current valuation evidence is weaker.

scoreRecord.thesis: MongoDB is converting broad developer adoption into accelerating revenue, cash flow and contracted demand while retaining AI workload optionality across Atlas and Enterprise Advanced.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Hyperscaler/native substitutes, consumption variability and high SBC can prevent strong operating growth from converting proportionally into per-share value.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: MongoDB Investor Day on September 29, 2026 and subsequent Atlas consumption/guidance checkpoints.

claims.claim: Q2 FY2027 revenue rose 30% to $771.8M and Atlas revenue rose about 29%.
RPO rose 91% and Q2 FCF was $137.6M.

risks.risk: SBC dilution, hyperscaler competition, consumption variability and expectation sensitivity remain material.

unknowns.unknown: Current valuation headroom is not sufficiently established to support a strong valuation score.
